newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SNB says M0 grew by annualised 9.2 pct in Q1 vs Q4.
newsitem.headline: SNB says M0 grew by annualised 9.2 pct in Q1 vs Q4.

text.p: The Swiss National Bank (SNB) said that its seasonally-adjusted central bank money aggregate M0 showed a growth on an annualised basis of 9.2 percent in the first quarter versus the fourth quarter of 1996.

"In the first quarter the seasonally-adjusted central bank money aggregate reached an average 32.481 billion Swiss francs. It overshot the level of the year-ago quarter by 6.0 percent, and the level of the fourth quarter 1996 by 2.2 percent (calculated on a one-year basis 9.2 percent)," the SNB said.
But the SNB said it expected M0 growth to slow in the second quarter.
"The central bank expects that the seasonally-ajdusted central bank money supply aggregate in the second quarter will average 32.9 billion francs," it said.

"This would mean an increase of 3.6 percent versus the fourth quarter of 1996. Calculated over the entire year, the seasonally-adjusted central bank money aggregate would likely reach 7.2 percent," the SNB said.

It said first quarter M0 growth, on a seasonally-adjusted basis, was somewhat more than 1.1 billion francs, or 3.5 percent, above its medium-term growth path, "and grew by significantly more than was forecast at the end of 1996."
"The mistake in the forecast, which is close to 700 million francs, is attributed largely to an accelerated growth in the notes in circulation," the SNB said.

"The source of this (growth acceleration) is still not known. The unexpectedly high need for liquidity by commercial banks, which showed up in a marked increase in sight deposits, also led to the mistake in the forecast," the SNB said.
It said during the course of the second quarter, notes in circulation, adjusted in terms of seasonal and fiscal factors, should grow only slightly.
"A signficant stimulation of notes in circulation tied to an economic upswing is still likely not to show up," the SNB said.
